I've been working this land for 55 years. I know Quzhou soil like I know my own hands. My wife and I, just the two of us now, we can't be doing anything too complicated. I'll stick to what I know works here.

**My thinking:**

The whole 5.2 mu rotates — wheat goes in after maize harvest in October, maize goes in after wheat harvest in June. Same land, same cycle I've been running since I was in my twenties.

For **wheat**, I'll rotary till after the maize harvest to break up the stubble and get a good seedbed. I always do a pre-winter irrigation — that's non-negotiable here in Quzhou, keeps the roots from freezing. Then I'll irrigate again at jointing and maybe once more at heading if it looks dry. I'll spread compound fertilizer as base before seeding, then top up with urea at jointing. Two rounds of spraying — once early for weeds, once later if I see rust or powdery mildew, which I usually do. I'll use the improved jinmai variety the seed station sells. I expect around 480 jin per mu — not the record yields they talk about at the experiment station, but reliable.

For **maize**, I direct-seed right into the wheat stubble. No sense tilling twice in one summer at my age. I'll use Zhengdan 958 — I've grown it for years, it doesn't surprise me. Summer rains usually handle most of the water, but I'll run the well pump at emergence if it's dry and again around tasseling. Corn borer shows up every year, so one insecticide pass, and herbicide early on. Maize gets more nitrogen than wheat — it's a hungry crop.

Two people, 5.2 mu, well irrigation, simple inputs. This is what feeds us and gives us a little to sell.
